Hi Karthik,

We're working through our vendor intake for Redwood ahead of procurement. Two asks from our InfoSec and Legal teams: 1) a mapped matrix showing which Redwood roles (service/engineers/support) have runtime access to PII fields; 2) an explicit cross-border transfer matrix that explains where tokenized/cache/KV data may be stored or routed (including any third-party subprocessors such as KMS providers or logging/monitoring services).

Hi Emily — thanks for the clear asks. We're preparing a short package that contains: the PII access-role matrix (who/why), a concise data-flow diagram showing where ephemeral token/KV cache and persistent telemetry land, and KMS custody notes.

Quick notes so expectations align:
- Runtime inference caches (KV/prefix caches) are ephemeral and confined to the serving region; they are not written to persistent storage except in rare debug traces (we'll annotate those exceptions).
- Persistent logs and audit trails are stored in region-bound storage per the DPA unless a customer requests cross-region analytics; we mark any such flows in the matrix.
- We use a third-party managed KMS for key storage (customer-managed keys supported for private deployments). We'll include which subprocessors are involved and whether they are in-scope for export controls.

I'll attach an initial draft by end of day; looping in Laura and Neha to confirm the PII field classification on our side.

Best,

Emily — attaching our package per your request. Summary below and quick answers to the specific asks.

Package contents (attached):
- pii-data-map-and-roles.xlsx (tabbed: PII fields, Roles & access, Access justification, Retention & region)
- redwood-dpa-kms-custody-appendix.pdf (KMS subprocessors, export & custody notes)
- dataflow-diagram.png (inline visual) — small, embedded in the PDF as well.

Quick answers:
1) Who has runtime access to PII fields?
- Roles with direct runtime access: inference-service (reads ephemeral inputs into memory), model-serving-op (Can rotate model config but cannot decrypt customer keys), support-ops (ticketed limited decrypt with approval). See XLS for row-level mapping.
2) Are any caches persisted or transferred cross-border?
- Default: KV/prefix caches are ephemeral and confined to the serving region and cleared per-session. Persistent telemetry and logs are region-bound by default. Any cross-region replication requires explicit customer opt-in and is annotated in the XLS.
3) KMS/export:
- We use Redwood-managed KMS for hosted deployments; for Private we support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own KMS). Exports are gated: operator decrypt capability is strictly limited and governed by a break-glass process (ticketing + 2nd approver). Appendix lists subprocessors and their locations.

Attachments: pii-data-map-and-roles.xlsx (contains the matrix), redwood-dpa-kms-custody-appendix.pdf (custody + subprocessors), dataflow-diagram.png (visual).

Let us know if you'd prefer a short walkthrough (15–20 mins) with Laura/Neha to step through the matrix.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Sales — Redwood Inference
